title: World news
intro: Ten selected stories on politics, economics, science, the environment and society, covering October 1–28, 2026. Ongoing developments are labelled accordingly.

items.title: A Nobel Prize for a new view of the universe
items.summary: The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences announced Francis Halzen as the 2026 Nobel laureate in Physics. It recognised his decisive contributions to the IceCube Observatory at the South Pole and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos from astrophysical sources.
items.whyItMatters: These particles help researchers study energetic events in the distant universe that are difficult to observe with other methods.

items.title: Navi Pillay awarded the Nobel Peace Prize
items.summary: The Norwegian Nobel Committee announced the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize for South African jurist Navi Pillay. It honours her work for peace and international law, including her service at international courts and as UN High Commissioner for Human Rights.
items.whyItMatters: The decision highlights the role of law and accountability in the peaceful resolution of international conflicts.

items.title: IMF forecasts uneven growth and higher inflation
items.summary: In its October outlook, the International Monetary Fund forecasts global growth of 3.1% in 2026 and 3.4% in 2027. It projects global inflation at 4.7% in 2026, falling to 4.1% in 2027; armed conflicts, trade disputes and high debt remain important risks.
items.whyItMatters: According to the IMF, the averages conceal major differences, with energy-importing economies outside the technology boom facing particular pressure.

items.title: EU and Ukraine open more accession chapters
items.summary: The EU and Ukraine opened negotiations on the internal market and on competitiveness and inclusive growth. The clusters cover areas including free movement, competition, consumer protection, taxation, education and research; progress in adopting and implementing EU rules will continue to be reviewed.
items.whyItMatters: This expands the concrete reform negotiations, but does not yet mean EU membership.

items.title: COP17 reviews progress on protecting nature
items.summary: The UN Biodiversity Conference COP17 takes place in Yerevan from October 19 to 30. Its agenda includes the first collective global review of progress under the Kunming-Montreal framework; the conference was still under way at this issue's October 28 cutoff.
items.whyItMatters: The review is intended to identify where further action is needed to reach the 2030 biodiversity goals.

items.title: Yemen: fighting threatens Taiz's water supply
items.summary: UNICEF warned on October 20 that escalating fighting and fuel shortages were threatening the water systems it supports in Taiz. UNICEF estimates that these systems serve about three million people, including at least 1.6 million children, while disrupted supply routes also put food and fuel supplies under pressure.
items.whyItMatters: Water-pump failures and poor sanitation can worsen an already strained health and nutrition situation.

items.title: Malaria vaccine price set to fall
items.summary: Gavi and UNICEF announced an agreement intended to cut the price of the RTS,S/AS01 malaria vaccine by about 40%, to €5.50 per dose. The lower price is expected in early 2027 and remains subject to regulatory and manufacturing milestones.
items.whyItMatters: The expected savings could ease pressure on vaccination programmes and help more children gain access.

items.title: WHO reports further spread of the Ebola outbreak
items.summary: In its October 23 situation report, WHO described continuing transmission of Bundibugyo ebolavirus in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and imported cases in Kenya and Nigeria. As of October 20, Kenya had reported nine cases, all in one linked cluster, with no evidence of transmission beyond that cluster according to WHO.
items.whyItMatters: Early detection, contact tracing and coordinated action across borders are particularly important for containment.

items.title: Brazil: Lula wins the presidential runoff
items.summary: Brazil's electoral court declared Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva the winner of the October 25 runoff with about 51.8% of the vote. His opponent Flávio Bolsonaro initially refused to concede and called for the result to be annulled.
items.whyItMatters: The result gives Lula a mandate for a fourth term, while the dispute over the outcome shapes the immediate political situation.

items.title: Greenhouse gases reach record levels again
items.summary: The WMO report published on October 27 records new highs in atmospheric CO₂, methane and nitrous oxide for 2025. The globally averaged CO₂ concentration was 426.8 ppm; the report describes accumulated concentrations rather than the emissions newly released in a single year.
items.whyItMatters: CO₂ remains in the atmosphere for a long time, so this accumulation influences the climate over decades and centuries.
